evidence: frontend/apps/mobile/src/hooks/useOfflineSupport.ts:419-427 — in processQueue's catch, an action whose replay returns a PERMANENT 4xx (executeQueuedAction marks it `permanent` for any 4xx that is NOT in RETRYABLE_HTTP_STATUSES {401,408,429}, i.e. 400/403/404/409/422/…) is handled by: `failed++; terminalFailureIds.add(action.id); console.error('Action permanently failed (4xx), dropping:', action);` — and terminalFailureIds are then EXCLUDED from the carried-forward queue at :479 (`(a) => !succeededIds.has(a.id) && !terminalFailureIds.has(a.id)`). So the queued action — which is offline-created USER CONTENT (a fault report, a meter reading, a message the user composed while offline) — is permanently deleted from AsyncStorage with no persisted record and no user-facing notification. The only trace is a dev-console line that never reaches a released build's user.

The failure is invisible to the user AND the app's own recovery affordance cannot recover it: components/sync/SyncProgressToast.tsx renders a Retry button whenever `isComplete && failed > 0` (:129) and PendingSyncIndicator.tsx shows a per-item retry for status 'failed' (:87). But the permanently-dropped items were already removed from the queue (:479), so tapping Retry re-runs processQueue over a queue that no longer contains them — a guaranteed no-op for exactly the items the '⚠ N failed' badge is telling the user to retry. The UI thus actively implies the lost content is recoverable when it has already been discarded.

Impact: a resident who reports a fault or submits a meter reading while offline is shown a success/'saved offline, will sync when online' confirmation (e.g. screens/faults/ReportFaultScreen.tsx queueForLater Alert 'faults.queuedTitle', screens/meters/MeterReadingScreen.tsx 'meters.savedOffline'), then — if the replay hits a 422 validation error or a 403 (e.g. a permission/tenant edge, a since-deleted building, a server-side validation the client did not mirror) — the content silently vanishes with no way for the user to learn it was lost or to re-enter it. This is a data-loss-visibility gap that the surrounding code was otherwise carefully written to avoid (the same file goes to great lengths NOT to drop transient/5xx failures, issues #1767/#2637).

Fix (landable in isolation, jest-expo coverable): instead of silently discarding permanent-4xx actions, either (a) move them to a persisted dead-letter list (a new AsyncStorage key in services/localCacheKeys) and surface a 'these offline items could not be synced' screen/toast with the failing action + server message so the user can re-enter or dismiss, and/or (b) at minimum emit a user-visible notification (not console.error) naming what was dropped and why, and stop showing a Retry affordance for items that are no longer in the queue. Confidence medium: the drop + dequeue + console-only + Retry-no-op chain is statically certain and traced end-to-end; the medium (not high) rating reflects that a permanent-4xx-on-replay outcome is not runtime-confirmed to be common in production.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/screens/faults/ReportFaultScreen.tsx:519-566 renders a full photo-attachment UX — camera + gallery pickers (pickImage), up to 5 photos (selectionLimit 5, :195/:200), in-place compression when over 10 MB (applyPhotos :211), thumbnail previews with remove buttons (:523-528), and warning copy — yet handleSubmit (:285) builds the CreateFaultVariables payload (:301-310) with only building_id/title/description/category/priority/location_description/idempotency_key and NEVER includes `photos`. The photos array (state at :96) is not referenced anywhere in the submit or queue path.

The omission is acknowledged in-code as unfinished: the comment at :297-300 says 'NOTE: `photos` holds local device URIs (compressed in-place when over 10 MB). Uploading attachments needs the presigned-URL pipeline (POST /faults/{id}/attachments), which has no shared mobile helper yet — tracked as a follow-up. The fault itself is created/queued here.' So the attachments are deliberately dropped, but nothing tells the user.

The user-facing copy actively promises an upload that never happens: locales/en.json 'faults.photosCompressedWarning' = '…were compressed to {{final}} MB so they upload faster…' and 'faults.photosStillLargeWarning' = '…so the upload may be slow or fail on a weak connection.' After submit the user sees 'faults.successSubmit' ('Fault reported successfully', Alert at :324) or the offline 'faults.queuedTitle' with no mention that the photos they attached, compressed and previewed were discarded. Photo evidence is exactly what makes a fault report actionable for a property manager, so silently dropping it while confirming success is a real data-integrity/trust problem, not a cosmetic one.

Fix (landable in isolation): either wire the attachment upload after the fault create resolves (POST /api/v1/faults/{id}/attachments via the presigned-URL pipeline; for the offline path, enqueue dependent attachment-upload actions keyed to the fault's temp localId, which useOfflineSupport already remaps to the server id — issue #1767) OR, as an honest interim, warn the user at submit time that photos are not yet uploaded (and/or hide the photo picker behind the missing capability) so no one believes evidence was filed when it was not. Confidence HIGH: the payload omission and the 'no shared mobile helper yet' comment are unambiguous and the reachable success/queued alerts contain no photo caveat — traced entirely within this one file.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/screens/meters/MeterReadingScreen.tsx:99-133 — handleSubmit's only validation is `if (!reading.trim()) { Alert.alert(...'meters.readingRequired'); return; }`. There is no numeric parse, no non-negative check, and no monotonic (>= previous reading) check. The raw string is placed verbatim into the queued/POSTed body: `reading: reading.trim()` (:111 / :126, endpoint POST /api/v1/meter-readings). A value like '', ' 12.3.4', '-5', '1,234', 'abc' (see below), or a fat-fingered extra digit is submitted as-is.

keyboardType="decimal-pad" (:224) only chooses the on-screen soft keyboard; it does NOT constrain the value. React Native TextInput still accepts PASTED text, hardware-keyboard input, and platform IMEs regardless of keyboardType, and decimal-pad permits multiple '.' separators on some Android IMEs — so non-numeric or malformed content can reach `reading` and be submitted. Contrast screens/meters/MeterDetailScreen.tsx:51-55, which defensively coerces incoming readings with a toNumber(Number.parseFloat) helper — the write path has no equivalent guard.

This compounds with the offline queue's silent permanent-4xx drop (see code-review-mobile-rn-offline-permanent-4xx-silent-drop): when offline, an unvalidated/malformed reading is queued, the user is shown 'meters.savedOffline / willSyncWhenOnline' success, and if the backend rejects the malformed value with a 422 on replay the reading is silently discarded — the user never learns their utility reading did not record. Even online, a lower-than-previous or mistyped reading corrupts consumption/billing calculations downstream.

Fix (small, jest-expo coverable): before enqueue/submit, parse the reading with Number.parseFloat, reject NaN / negative / non-finite with a localized error Alert (mirroring the existing 'meters.readingRequired' pattern), optionally warn when the new value is below the last known reading, and send a normalized numeric value rather than the raw string. Confidence medium; score_delta 1 (Low) because decimal-pad mitigates casual non-numeric entry, so the residual risk is paste/IME/format/monotonic rather than a guaranteed crash or security issue — a data-quality/validation gap.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/queryKeys.ts:354-392 — `AUTHED_QUERY_KEY_ROOTS` is the allow-list that logout() iterates to purge per-user cache, and its own doc comment (:346-350) states it 'must cover ALL tenant-/user-scoped caches' and that such caches 'must never survive logout on a shared workstation' (#712 replaced the blunt queryClient.clear() with this scoped removal). The list is materially incomplete. A sweep of the query-key factories actually mounted in ppt-web (each defines `all: ['<root>']`) versus this allow-list shows these authed roots are MISSING from the purge: community, disputes, iot, outages, leases, voting, plus (defined in @ppt/api-client and reachable) visitors, packages, violations, my-units, compliance, esignature, portfolio-performance, registries, templates, integrations, syndication, ecosystem, oauth-grants, mfa. Each of community/disputes/iot/outages/leases/voting is a mounted ppt-web route group (frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/{community,disputes,iot,outages,leases,voting}.tsx) whose pages populate a TanStack Query cache under that root.

Auth path traced end-to-end: logout() at frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:614-637 clears localStorage + React state, then loops `for (const root of AUTHED_QUERY_KEY_ROOTS) queryClient.removeQueries({ queryKey: [root] })` (:624-626) — a prefix-match purge. Any cached query whose first key segment is NOT in the allow-list is left intact. So after User A views e.g. /disputes (mediation chat threads, resolution PII), /leases (tenant PII), or /community (neighbour posts/marketplace), then logs out, those caches persist in the shared queryClient; User B logging in on the same browser is served User A's cached tenant/user-scoped data until each query happens to refetch. This is the exact cross-session data-leak class the list was created to prevent — a privacy/isolation defect on a shared-workstation path.

Confirmed drift example (not just omission): the list contains 'votes' (:360) but the live factory root is `['voting']` (frontend/packages/api-client/src/voting/hooks.ts, `all: ['voting']`), and voting.tsx is a mounted ppt-web route — so the voting cache is never purged despite an entry that looks like it covers it. Landable frontend-only remedy: extend AUTHED_QUERY_KEY_ROOTS with the missing mounted roots (correcting 'votes' -> 'voting' or adding both), and add a guard test that asserts every `*.all` key-factory root imported into ppt-web appears in AUTHED_QUERY_KEY_ROOTS so the list cannot silently drift again. Verifiable via `pnpm --filter @ppt/web typecheck` + a Vitest test that seeds queries for each root, calls logout(), and asserts getQueryCache() is empty of authed roots. Confidence high: traced login -> cache population (mounted route groups) -> logout purge loop -> allow-list omission.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/contexts/WebSocketContext.tsx:61-68 — `categoryToQueryKeys` maps a `notification.created` payload.category to the query roots to invalidate. It covers only 6 categories: announcements, faults, votes, messages, documents, financial. The backend enum NotificationCategory (backend/crates/common/src/notifications/mod.rs:75-121, `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]`) has 8 variants whose wire strings are: announcements, faults, votes, messages, community, financial, documents, system. So `community` and `system` are absent from the frontend map.

Real stale-data miss for `community`: backend maps NotificationEvent::CommunityEvent -> NotificationCategory::Community (backend/crates/common/src/notifications/events.rs:285) which serializes to "community". When that notification.created frame arrives, WebSocketContext.tsx:344-350 does `categoryToQueryKeys[category]` -> undefined, so `queryKeys` falls back to `['notifications']` only and the `['community']` cache is never invalidated. `['community']` is a live ppt-web cache: frontend/packages/api-client/src/community/hooks.ts:28 defines `communityKeys.all = ['community']` (posts/events/groups/marketplace lists) and community.tsx is a mounted route group. Net effect: a new community event pushes a notification but the community feed/events list stays stale until a manual refetch — the map's own comment (:55-59) claims it refreshes 'both the notification list and the announcements list', but the community domain silently falls through.

Landable frontend-only remedy: add `community: ['community']` to categoryToQueryKeys (and decide whether `system`/EmergencyAlert needs any list root — likely notifications-only, so document it explicitly to close the gap). Ideally add a small unit test / type-level check that every NotificationCategory wire value is either mapped or explicitly allow-listed, so future backend categories can't silently regress realtime sync. Verifiable via `pnpm --filter @ppt/web typecheck` + a Vitest test dispatching a `notification.created` frame with category 'community' and asserting onEntityEvent is called with a queryKeys array containing 'community'. Confidence high: traced the CommunityEvent -> Community -> "community" serialization on the backend and the undefined lookup on the frontend against the live ['community'] cache root.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/api.ts:370 — `export default getApiClient();` runs at module import time, eagerly constructing an axios instance with DEFAULT config (no getToken, no onUnauthorized, DEFAULT_BASE_URL). AuthProvider later calls configureApiClient() (contexts/AuthContext.tsx:380), which does `apiInstance = createAxiosInstance(config)` (api.ts:348) — a brand-new instance — so the eagerly-created default export is immediately orphaned and can never receive a custom baseURL/timeout passed to configureApiClient. It is a latent footgun: any future `import apiClient from '../lib/api'` binds permanently to that pre-configuration instance, bypassing configureApiClient's baseURL and the reset lifecycle (resetApiClient() at :356 nulls apiInstance but the default-exported object reference lives on).

Confirmed unused today: no default-style importer of lib/api exists (grep of frontend/apps/ppt-web/src for `import <ident> from '.../lib/api'` returns 0 non-test hits), and lib/index.ts (:8-18) re-exports only the named symbols (getApiClient, configureApiClient, resetApiClient, ...), not the default. So the line is a dead eager side-effect at import time plus a trap for future callers. Landable frontend-only remedy: delete the `export default getApiClient();` line (callers already use the named getApiClient()), or, if a default is desired for ergonomics, make it a lazy accessor rather than an eager call so it always resolves to the configured singleton. Verifiable via `pnpm --filter @ppt/web typecheck` + `pnpm --filter @ppt/web test`. Confidence medium: static analysis confirms the orphaning and zero current default-import consumers, but severity is low precisely because nothing imports it yet — this is a smell/footgun cleanup, not an active production break.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/workflow-automation/pages/AutomationRulesPage.tsx:56-72 - three state-changing handlers await a mutateAsync with NO try/catch and NO rendered error state: confirmDelete (:56-61) -> await deleteRule.mutateAsync(deleteConfirm.id) then setDeleteConfirm(null); handleToggle (:63-68) -> await updateRule.mutateAsync({id, data:{isEnabled}}); handleRun (:70-72) -> await runRule.mutateAsync(rule.id). deleteRule/updateRule/runRule come from @ppt/api-client (useDeleteAutomationRule/useUpdateAutomationRule/useRunAutomationRule, imported :11-13,:44-46).

None of the three mutations' .error is rendered anywhere in the file: grep for deleteRule./updateRule./runRule./.error/.isError in AutomationRulesPage.tsx returns only deleteRule.isPending (:303 disabled, :306 'Deleting...' label) — the pending state is wired but the error state is not. So on a rejected request (permission denied, 4xx/5xx, network) the async handler's promise rejects unhandled and the user gets zero feedback.

confirmDelete has an extra defect: because setDeleteConfirm(null) is on the line AFTER the awaited mutateAsync (:58->:59), a rejected delete skips the state reset, leaving the delete-confirmation modal stuck open with no error message and no way to tell the delete failed. The manager reasonably assumes it worked (or retries into a second rejection).

The correct pattern exists on the sibling CreateRulePage in the SAME feature: CreateRulePage.tsx:62-66 renders {createRule.error && (...)} to surface create failures. AutomationRulesPage simply omits the equivalent for delete/toggle/run. Fix (low-risk): render deleteRule.error/updateRule.error/runRule.error inline (mirroring CreateRulePage), and move setDeleteConfirm(null) into an onSuccess / finally so the modal always closes appropriately.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/workflow-automation/pages/CreateRulePage.tsx:18-19 - handleSave receives rule: Partial<AutomationRule> from the RuleBuilder and immediately casts it to the full required type as it crosses the create-mutation API boundary: `await createRule.mutateAsync(rule as AutomationRule)`. The `as AutomationRule` assertion silences the compiler even though the value is typed Partial<> — every field the AutomationRule interface marks required (and that RuleBuilder did not populate) can be undefined at runtime while the type system now claims it is present.

This defeats the one compile-time guarantee that the create payload is complete: if RuleBuilder emits a partial rule (missing trigger, empty actions, etc.) the POST goes out as if well-formed, so validation is entirely deferred to the server (best case a 422 surfaced via createRule.error :62; worse case a malformed rule persisted if the server is lenient). The type-safe fix is to type useCreateAutomationRule's input as the actual create-request DTO (partial-by-design) or to validate/assemble a complete AutomationRule in RuleBuilder before onSave, rather than lying to the compiler with `as`.

Matches the skill's frontend pattern 'TypeScript cast that crosses an API boundary'. Net-new (no prior ppt-web-ui signal covers this file). Low severity, confidence medium (static-only; the concrete impact depends on whether RuleBuilder enforces completeness, which was not runtime-verified).

fn validate_image_or_link_url is duplicated VERBATIM in two public-endpoint route modules: routes/reports.rs:38 (guards report attachment URLs at submit_report:219) and routes/users.rs:28 (guards profile_image_url at update_me:357). The two copies are byte-identical apart from the length-cap constant name (reports.rs MAX_URL_LEN=2048 vs users.rs MAX_PROFILE_URL_LEN=2048 — same value): both parse with url::Url::parse and allow only http/https schemes to block javascript:/data:/file: stored-XSS payloads that the frontend later renders in /.

Both copies carry a now-STALE comment justifying the inline duplication: reports.rs:35-37 and users.rs:23-25 each say 'Inlined locally ... once the auth-hardening branch lands a shared `url_validator` module this should be swapped for the import.' That shared module ALREADY EXISTS on the reviewed tree: backend/servers/reality-server/src/util/url_validator.rs defines pub fn validate_fetch_url (util/mod.rs:7 re-exports it) and it is already imported and used by routes/agency_imports.rs:7. So the premise of the 'once it lands' TODO is satisfied, yet the two inline copies were never consolidated.

Impact (maintainability with a security-adjacent edge, hence low/+1): the reality-server public/anonymous URL-acceptance policy is now defined in THREE independent places with two different intents — util::validate_fetch_url (scheme + private-IP/SSRF + length, for server-fetched feed URLs) and two copies of validate_image_or_link_url (scheme + length, for frontend-rendered URLs). A future hardening of the frontend-rendered policy (e.g. blocking a newly-dangerous scheme, tightening the length cap, or adding host allow-listing) must be applied to both inline copies in lockstep; a change to only one silently drifts the report-attachment and profile-image code paths apart on an XSS-defense surface. There is NO active bug today — update_me and submit_report both correctly invoke their local validator — this is a consolidation/DRY finding.

Fix (low-risk): promote a single validate_display_url (scheme + length, distinct from the SSRF-oriented validate_fetch_url) into util/url_validator.rs beside the existing helper, replace the two inline copies with a shared import, and delete the stale 'once it lands on main' comments. NET-NEW: not covered by any prior reality-server signal (09-24 filed 0 findings) and orthogonal to the documented DNS-rebinding fetch-time follow-up. Confidence medium: the verbatim duplication, the stale comment, and the already-present shared module are objectively confirmed by static read; the drift risk is latent (no current defect).
